text:
- chief complaint: bilateral elbow pain, worse on the right, for about a year and a half, with the patient reporting heavy weightlifting.
- history of present illness: new-onset bilateral medial elbow pain for about 1.5 years, worse with arm/hand use, not relieved by icing, and partially relieved by ibuprofen 800 mg three times daily. X-rays showed no fractures or bony misalignment. Diagnosed with medial epicondylitis.
- physical examination: pain on medial palpation and with flexion/extension, worse on the right; mildly limited extension; pain with supination but not pronation; normal sensation and equal pulses in the extremities; no lateral pain.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: bilateral elbow pain, worse on the right, aggravated by use, no relief from ice.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: MRI of the elbow to be scheduled soon; whole blood injection (autologous blood therapy) planned in the next couple of weeks, pending MRI results.
